overview: This resolution, passed by both the House and Senate, allows Emancipation Hall in the U.S. Capitol Visitor Center to be used on September 3, 2025, for a ceremony presenting Congressional Gold Medals to the Harlem Hellfighters. The Harlem Hellfighters were the 369th Infantry Regiment, an African American unit that fought with distinction in World War I; Congress awarded them its highest civilian honor in a 2021 law. The Architect of the Capitol, the office that manages the Capitol buildings and grounds, sets the conditions for preparing the hall. Both chambers had agreed to it as of July 29, 2025, when the Senate notified the House of its approval.
for: Supporters say holding the ceremony in the Capitol gives fitting recognition to soldiers who served bravely despite facing discrimination at home.
against: Critics say the resolution is procedural and symbolic: it only reserves a room for a ceremony and doesn't change any law or spending.
